title: AI dialogue game, but it's actually fun
author: Affectionate_Key_217
selftext:
Hey everyone,

I started developing an AI-powered game about two years ago based on dialogues. Now that the first phase is finally complete, I’ve noticed a massive barrier and backlash from the gaming community when it comes to accepting games that use AI.

It makes sense, I think. We've seen a flood of half-baked, boring, or flat-out messy AI games - though we have some good ones too. On paper, having "unlimited freedom" to talk to a character sounds incredible. But five minutes in, you realize they have zero personality, repeat the same generic lines, and get you stuck in an infinite conversation loop that does absolutely nothing to progress your investigation, and the gameplay ends up just boring.

That's why I wanted to share my project with you guys. I tried to build something genuinely fun using AI by creating a "Key Information" mechanic.

Instead of letting the AI run completely wild, each suspect has a specific set of secrets you need to pry out of them. You investigate the crime scene, collect physical evidence, and interrogate the characters to unlock these secrets. Once you discover enough key info, you can fill out the final case report—which requires paying close attention to the tiny details of each answer to deduce what actually happened.

The cases are inspired by classic mystery and horror literature. To make sure the game doesn't feel like a soulless ChatGPT skin, all the art and environments were hand-drawn by a professional illustrator to capture the macabre, dark atmosphere of vintage horror comics. Since it’s an Open Beta, some of the detailed close-ups of the evidence are currently placeholders, but our illustrator will have them finalized for the official release.

If you have some spare time to check it out, the game actually turned out even more fun than I originally expected. I would love to get your brutal, honest feedback—even if it's to tell me that it actually sucks!

It's currently in Open Beta on the Google Play Store, and we're giving out 100 free credits so you can test the conversation limits.

Here is the Google Play link:

[https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.pmakers.games.folio.detective](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.pmakers.games.folio.detective)



Thanks for reading, and let me know if you manage to crack the case!
